paper_metadata.title: Creep properties of annealed Zr–Nb–O and stress-relieved Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe cladding tubes and their performance comparison

evidence.quote: Creep properties of annealed Zr–Nb–O and stress-relieved Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe cladding tubes were studied and compared.
The creep rates of the annealed Zr–Nb–O alloy were found to be greater than those of the stress-relieved Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe alloy.
Zr–Nb–O cladding tubes were heat-treated at 560 /C176C for 5 h
Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe alloy cladding tubes were stress-relieved at 460 /C176C for 7 h after ﬁnal cold pilgering.

evidence.quote: dislocation networks and pile-ups around the precipitates are found in the Zr–Nb–O matrix.
The stress-relieved Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe alloy was observed to have the ultimate tensile and yield strengths /C24 40% greater than those of the annealed Zr–Nb–O alloy.
the steady-state creep rates of the Zr–Nb–O alloy tubes are relatively higher than those of the Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe alloy
the total creep strain until fracture in Zr–Nb–O was in the range of 0.45–0.55 whereas that for Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe was in the range of 0.35–0.42.
the total creep strain until fracture in Zr–Nb–O was in the range of 0.45–0.55 whereas that for Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe was in the range of 0.35–0.42.
the stress exponent n remains constant (5–7) in the stress range of the present study for Zr–Nb–O
it decreases from 6.5 to 7.5 in the lower stress region to /C24 4.2 in the higher stress region for Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe
it decreases from 6.5 to 7.5 in the lower stress region to /C24 4.2 in the higher stress region for Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe
The activation energy for creep deformation is in the range of between 240 and 260 kJ/mol for the Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe alloy
while it is in the range of between 240 and 280 kJ/mol for the Zr–Nb–O alloy
The rate controlling mechanism for Zr–Nb–O alloy is thought to be the dislocation climb controlled creep in which the stress exponent is typically in the range of 5–7 independent of the stress level.
The reduction of stress exponent at high stresses in Zr–Nb–Sn–Fe can be explained in terms of the dynamic solute–dislocation effect caused by Sn atoms.
The slightly greater creep activation energy in Zr–Nb–O is thought to be attributed to the lower contribution of grain boundary diffusion due to a lager grain size.
